topic: What if you could switch off sleep?
part: Chapter 4 of 6: the first crack, school and the stairs (long-form, ~55 s)
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SWITCH OFF SLEEP?
previous_text: She asks how. You put a finger to your lips. Secret.

script.text: At school, you're unbeatable. Every question. Every quiz.
Mo can't figure out how you're always this awake. He's on his third energy drink. You're on zero.
Teachers start calling on you just to watch you get it right.
Day three. You still don't feel tired. But something's slipping.
You write the answer on the board. The right answer… to yesterday's question.
Then, on the stairs, the world blinks.
Mo catches you. He says you were asleep. Standing up. You don't remember any of it.
It has a name: a microsleep. Your brain grabs a few seconds of sleep, and it doesn't ask first. That's real.

science.claim: A microsleep is a brief, unintended episode of sleep lasting a few seconds, most likely after sleep loss, and the person often doesn't notice it
science.working: no number in the narration; 'a few seconds' matches the definitions (a fraction of a second up to about 15-30 s); 'half a second. Gone.' is the story's own lapse, within that range
science.source: Sleep Foundation, 'Microsleep: What Is It, What Causes It, and Is It Safe?' (sleepfoundation.org/sleep-disorders/microsleep); NHLBI (NIH), 'Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency: health effects' (nhlbi.nih.gov/health/sleep-deprivation/health-effects): microsleep is brief moments of sleep while normally awake, you can't control it and may not be aware of it; Poudel et al., 'Losing the struggle to stay awake', NeuroImage 2014

shots.note: the class at dusk: the board full of formulas, every one solved; you at your desk, hand already up, sure
quiz papers slap down one after another, each stamped A+
Mo slumped on the desk next to you, eyes half shut; you upright, wide awake, eyes glowing
three energy-drink cans on Mo's desk; his hand drags the third one in; gulp
you, nothing on your desk, a cool little shrug; a tag: 0
the teacher at the board points at you; a kid turns to look; you answer, smug
the wall calendar: day 3 gets its red cross; DAY 3
you, still glowing, one slow heavy blink; the glow flickers; a flicker of worry
you at the board writing the answer in chalk, confident
the board: the answer is to YESTERDAY's question, a big red X; kids laugh; you, oops
you walk down the stairs (walkPhase), mid-step: the screen cuts to black for 12 frames, silence
you pitch forward off the step, arms flailing
Mo grabs you under the arms; you hang there dizzy, stars circling
you, still held up by Mo, dazed: you don't remember any of it; the stars fade
a day as a bar: AWAKE runs, a few seconds of SLEEP cut in without asking; REAL
